prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: Brain activity was measured using high-density electroencephalography at the start, middle, and end of the study while participants completed a visual reaction task that required them to either respond or withhold a response.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The training did not change the size of the early P1 or later P3 brain signals.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Participants in the dual-task training group showed growing N1 brain signals, which suggests better attentional selection, and larger prefrontal P2 signals, which indicates improved integration of stimuli and actions.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The control group, which received only motor training, did not show similar changes in these brain signals.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: An exploratory index showed a consistent and progressive pattern of coordinated brain adaptation in the dual-task training group across different stages of processing.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The results suggest that some of the brain vulnerabilities associated with frailty might be partially reversed by training that combines cognitive and motor tasks.
facts.subject: humans
